title: Six-class rho on secp256k1 with generated AArch64 batch loops (126.3651)

claims.statement: For uniform full-production secp256k1 Q=[x]P, the classical cold six-class negation+GLV parallel Pollard rho attack specified in proof.md halts on every run after at most 2^126.3651 target-group-operation equivalents: a global meter charges every action before it runs. The ordinary step is not charged as a reference addition plus allowance; it is charged at its counted scalar AArch64 instructions, 765 instructions = 0.765 units of C=1000 (counted 111 + 523 instructions per walk for the two loop passes, hand-scheduled AArch64 assembly emitted by kernels/gen_loops.py as kernels/secp_loops.s, executed natively on AArch64 and by an interpreter in experiment.py against affine arithmetic, plus 129 instruction allowances for the class bookkeeping rows, 763 in all); traversal costs 0.795 and doubling at most 1.1 (967 instructions bound), and no reference operation is also charged. Under the disclosed heuristic H1 (random-mapping collision time with slowdown allowance kappa=1.02, floor p0=0.3953 at S_ops/kappa), the chance of recovery is greater than 0.3901 after a Markov early-halt bound below 0.00516 and all other loss events. The slowdown allowance is supported by a toy census of 162,316 trials (slowdown +1.13% +/- 0.17% at q25, +0.22% +/- 0.20% at q29). Peak memory is below 2^72 bytes; preprocessing is capped at 2^59 units and included; no nonuniform advice. The walk, class key, canonical-index rule, cycle handling, phases, storage and bookkeeping rows are those of submission 061e00ca (six-class-rho-secp-counted-v7, 126.403), itself built on 30f6f34e, 98e7729c, b52f8806, a9f1a6fe, 3682292, 758d8df6 and 189ebc42; all are credited dependencies but no prior verdict is a mathematical premise. This is an analytical, heuristic bound, not a practical break.

experiments.purpose: Part A: production secp256k1 checks of the walk identities and truncated canonical-index rule; Part B: a scaled sequential toy pipeline on configured subgroups of y^2=x^3+7 with an unreduced subgroup-order check, a T_c census, node routing, and a long-trail trap test; kernels: limb-for-limb Python ports of the field kernels checked against big integers and affine secp256k1, instruction counts parsed from the shipped AArch64 assembly, and the work-meter ledger recomputed. The toy run does not meter production instructions or implement 2^20 concurrent walks.
